title: Linear-Time Implies Polynomial-Time
statement: Let $f$ be a function from bit strings to bit strings. If there exist a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet and a natural number $C$ such that, on every input of length $n$, the machine computes $f$ within $C(n+1)$ steps, then $f$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: There is a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet
The machine computes $f$ within $C(n+1)$ steps on every input
replaced:
Let $f$ be a function from binary strings to binary strings. If there exist a finite
multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet and a constant $C$ such that the
machine computes $f$ within $C\cdot(n+1)$ steps on every input of length $n$, then
$f$ is polynomial-time computable.
